questions.question: The step notes put the source tax details (denomination, spouse works, children: steps 6/6a) before the cross-border questions (step 7). A Liechtenstein resident who returns daily, or expects at most 45 non-return days, gets 'in principle no source tax liability' and no tariff code. So their denomination, spouse employment and children answers are not needed (AC-05.7.3 shows them as '–'). Should these employees be asked the Liechtenstein questions first and then skip denomination, spouse employment and children? Or are those answers asked and then discarded on submission? Either way the order of the flow changes, and so does what is collected (G-01 data minimisation).

Is the email address typed in for the copy recorded for HR or kept after the email is sent, or only used to send it? Does the copy itself list the 'send me a copy' answer and the email address as submitted answers? The spec says 'nothing more' but does not say whether these two closing items count as answers.

What date checks apply? Can the first working day be in the past, or how far in the future? Is there a minimum or maximum age for the employee's date of birth, and any check on the spouse's date of birth? The ACs only say 'required, DD.MM.YYYY'. A wrong first working day directly gives a wrong insurance start date.

The rule 'How a child counts for the tariff' and the Single-parent H rule say a child counts as an H child when it 'lives in the household and the employee has sole custody or is the main contributor'. Yet row 21 (and AC-06.3.3) count a minor child NOT in the household as an H child (single parent with custody, alternating care, employee is the main contributor → H1N). Which is right: the plain-language rule or the decision table? The H/P letter depends on it.

The certificate of residence question is phrased two ways. information.md asks whether the employee 'has' a certificate; AC-07.2.2 asks whether they 'have provided' it (to HR). Which one is meant? An employee who has the certificate but has not handed it in yet would answer differently, and the answer switches between the cross-border and normal tariff.

The cross-border answers are 'what they expect for the year' / 'in the calendar year'. Which year is meant for an employee who starts late in the year (e.g. in December): the current calendar year, the first full year, or the next 12 months? Without this the question wording cannot be finalised.

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the normal code is 'marked subject to the double taxation agreement'. Is this case also flagged for HR, like the 'in principle no liability' case? Or is it only a note on the code? Two different outcomes have to be recorded.
Is there a maximum number of children an employee can enter? The calculator limit is unknown, and the tariff code holds a single digit. What should the result be when 10 or more children count?

For married employees, 'Has children' includes the spouse's/partner's children. For a stepchild, whose custody, maintenance contribution and 'other parent' do the custody and contribution questions refer to? The question wording has to make this clear, or answers will be inconsistent.
HR words the permit reminder. Who supplies the final text, and by when? It also has to work for Swiss citizens living abroad. Without the text the story cannot be finished or accepted.

Before submission, can the employee leave the questionnaire and come back later with their answers kept? Is there a deadline, or a point at which an unsubmitted questionnaire's answers are deleted? 'Kept while going back and forth' does not say whether answers survive across sessions, which matters for data minimisation.

Should the employee see the derived insurance start date (or the source tax result) anywhere in the questionnaire before or after submitting? Or is it only recorded for HR/the fund? The copy explicitly excludes these values, but nothing is said about showing them on screen.

The AC-01.2.1 example shows the country as '–' for the Switzerland row but 'required' for the Germany row, although the country is always required. Similarly, US-03.3 shows the spouse's date of birth as '–' for Married but 'required' for Registered partnership. Examples elsewhere also mix 'asked' and 'required'. Please correct the example tables so they can be used as test cases.

The trace check notes that the Liechtenstein example treats the employee as 'subject to source tax: yes', while D-007 gives them 'in principle no source tax liability'. What should be recorded for HR as 'subject to source tax' for these employees: yes, no, or a separate status?

already_flagged: OQ-canton-abroad: what to enter in the fund's 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and whether it means residence or work
OQ-civil-status-partnership: how the fund wants registered partnership and separated employees registered
OQ-spouse-dob-other-status: whether the fund needs the spouse's date of birth or other fields for Divorced/Widowed
OQ-calculator-coverage: computed tariff codes for unexplored calculator paths (A/B/H residence block, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N)
OQ-child-paths-undetermined: outcome of child-answer combinations not shown by the calculator, and whether HR determines the code in the meantime

tech_leaks.quote: are derived again from the latest answers; no history of earlier values is kept
tech_leaks.why: This makes a storage/retention decision for all derived results. The source (D-033) only says no history is kept of earlier first working days; the spec's own trace check notes this extension is not backed.

tech_leaks.quote: The expression evaluates one child; the rule applies to each child.
tech_leaks.why: It refers to an implementation artifact (an 'expression') instead of the business rule. The same applies to 'The expression covers a single child; with several children the counts are added up.'

tech_leaks.quote: Lonio records that the tariff code cannot be computed yet instead of a possibly wrong code, so the case stays visible for HR
tech_leaks.why: This prescribes system behaviour that no stakeholder or decision asked for; the trace check says the cited facts do not require it. The open question still offers 'HR determines the code' as an alternative.

tech_leaks.quote: the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child
tech_leaks.why: This describes interaction mechanics (add/remove child blocks, copied from the calculator UI). The business need is only that each child's answers are collected; how the employee enters several children is a UI choice.
